name: Mysuru
headline: Mysuru had the state's most child-marriage complaints in six months of 2024.
summary: Between April and September 2024 Mysuru received 105 child-marriage complaints, the most in the state, with 36 marriages carried out and 69 prevented. A legislative reply also named single-parent households among the reasons for dropout in Mysuru and five other educational districts.

reasons.detail: 105 complaints in six months of 2024, 36 marriages carried out and 69 prevented, ending girls' schooling.
A legislative reply named single-parent households among the reasons for school dropout in Mysuru and five other educational districts.
In some backward rural communities, girls are kept from school after attaining puberty as parents seek marriage; most identified out-of-school children were girls.

reasons.factor: Low awareness in SC/ST, minority blocks
reasons.detail: Dropouts were higher in educational blocks with larger Muslim and SC/ST populations, which officials linked to lack of awareness about education.
Prolonged Covid school closure and lack of devices were blamed for rising dropouts and child labour, prompting a house-to-house survey of children aged 6-14 in Mysuru city.
An NGO founder reported about 170 child-marriage cases in Mysuru district over seven months of 2020, with school shutdowns removing meals and protection.
In HD Kote, residential schools for Jenu Kuruba and other communities stood empty after Covid; no electricity or phones, and contract-teacher staffing problems hampered learning.
Mysuru's SSLC rank fell to 15th in 2025 and 20th in 2026 despite higher pass rates; the DDPI promised corrective analysis. Link to exits is not evidenced.

responses.text: The state offers Rs 50,000 to gram panchayats that prevent child marriage.
Mysuru City Corporation, with the education and child welfare departments, ran a house-to-house app survey from mid-January to mid-February 2021 to identify out-of-school children aged 6-14.
Free education, hostel access and financial assistance exist for ST students in Mysuru, though an expert says they are insufficient without tackling structural barriers.
District DDPI said the department would analyse the 2025 SSLC results and implement corrective strategies to improve.
